title: Coen on Loss to Texans: “I’ve Got a Lot of Confidence in This Team.” | Press Conference
headline: Coen says Brian Thomas Jr. was part of the plan to get more involved early, and praises Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s hard running, though Thomas's lack of second-half snaps was left unresolved.
summary: Coen said the 34-31 loss to Houston was not good enough and that the team needs to review the film, especially the penalties, a punt-safety mistake, and the passing game. He said the wet conditions and a dropped or misfired deep ball made some plays hard to make, and that the offense has to find a way to convert in those moments. He described getting Brian Thomas Jr. more involved early as part of the game plan, credited him with critical plays on both sides of the ball, and said he competed well. Asked about Thomas's lack of second-half snaps, Coen answered only that players have to step up week to week. He praised Chris Rodriguez Jr. for running hard against a good Houston run defense, even though the yards were not what the team wanted. Coen said he has a lot of confidence in the group and will not change the process, while acknowledging the need to clean up specific areas. He called the London trip a first-class experience and said the loss was disappointing mainly because the fans did not get a win.

topics.detail: Coen said penalties, including a wiped-out touchdown for holding and a late defensive pass interference call, hurt the team. He said operations were cleaner overall, and that a substitution mistake on a fourth-and-one punt-safe situation was his team's error.
Coen said the wet weather and a few drops or uncertain deep throws made some offensive plays difficult to evaluate. He said the team needs to make those plays in key moments.
Coen said he has a lot of confidence in the team, is extremely proud of how it fought back from ten-point deficits, and does not plan to change its process.
Coen called the London trip first class and said the team handled the experience with professionalism. He was disappointed not to win in front of the fans.
